answer: The opal test I would run is Lapidary drilled bead assay witnessed by the cutters ledger: each drilled bead is a mine assay countersigned by the warden, so a farm must cut a hundred real stones by hand, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the dawn of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head. The pigment is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
